You know that random moment where you suddenly think:

“Wait… when did I last water the plant?”

Or take the vitamins. Or call your parents. Or replace the air filter. Or feed the sourdough starter that may or may not still be alive.

Most productivity apps respond to this by screaming at you with streaks, charts, and guilt notifications.

Just Did does the opposite.

Just Did is a calm little app built around one simple question:
“When did I last do that?”

No streaks to protect. No pressure. No “you failed your routine” energy.

Just a simple way to log the things you’ve already done and quietly remember them later.

The interaction is weirdly satisfying too:
• Tap and hold a task card to mark it done
• No checklists, forms, or clutter
• Optional reminders if it’s been “a while”
• Flexible cadences like every 3 hours, 4 days, or 2 weeks
• Shared Spaces for couples, roommates, coworkers, or friends
• See who handled what without assigning tasks or nagging people
• Personal tasks stay on-device for privacy
• Use locally without even creating an account if you want

Honestly, it feels less like a productivity app and more like a soft memory extension for real life.

Perfect for people who hate traditional habit trackers but still want some sense of order without the pressure.

How to Redeem:
Open the app and click Spaces Pro. Click Redeem Code and enter the code INDIEAPPSANTA

Once you start using it, your brain stops wasting energy trying to remember tiny life maintenance tasks all day.

This one’s surprisingly comforting.

You open your photo gallery… and suddenly realize you haven’t touched it in months.

A thousand photos. Screenshots you forgot. 12 blurry shots of the same sunset. Storage creeping up. Memories buried under clutter.

Picmori fixes that.

Picmori lets you swipe through your photos one by one, keep the ones you love, let go of the rest.
It’s simple. Swipe right to save. Swipe left to delete. Done.

A few things that make it feel surprisingly satisfying:
• Detects duplicates and similar photos automatically
• Group shots from the same burst or series for easy selection
• Track session stats: see how many photos you reviewed, kept, and deleted
• Free up storage without losing what matters
• Works fully offline, all processing happens on your device
• Relive forgotten memories as you declutter
It’s basically a tiny, playful spring cleaning session for your gallery every time you open the app.

How to Redeem the Promo

Perfect for anyone drowning in old screenshots, repeats, or blurry bursts, without risking the photos you actually love.

Less clutter. More memories that matter.

Today’s indie app worth studying:

(Not Boring) Weather

Most people wouldn’t touch this category.

Apple already has a Weather app.
The App Store already has hundreds more.

But Andy Allen still built one.

Not by adding 50 new features.

By making checking the weather feel insanely well-crafted.

Animations.
Sound.
Haptics.
Tiny details everywhere.

It became an Apple Editors’ Choice app and helped Not Boring win an Apple Design Award.

Sometimes a crowded category isn’t the problem.

A boring product is.

i shipped a new budgetwise update.

everyone sees the siri expense logging feature.

what they don’t see is that i also changed the app name, subtitle, improved the app store listing, and localized subscription pricing for different markets.

as an engineer, it’s easy to think your job ends when the feature is finished.

building an indie app has taught me that’s only half the job.

sometimes the biggest improvements aren’t new features.

they’re making it easier for the right people to discover the product in the first place.

let’s see what the numbers look like over the next few weeks.

You’ve made dozens of critical decisions today. Cleared meetings. Solved problems.

Then you open the fridge and hit a wall. Traditional dieting forces you into an exhausting second job of manual logging, food weighing, and calorie tracking.

So you give up, open a delivery app, and bleed cash on high-fat convenience food. That is a vicious convenience cycle draining your wallet and your health.

PicMeal breaks it by completely automating your kitchen.

Point your phone camera, snap a photo of your raw ingredients, and let our engine handle the homework. No manual typing. No guessing.

Clean Features Built to Eliminate Planning Fatigue:
Vision Scanner: Photo-map your open fridge or pantry inventory instantly with zero data entry.
AI Recipe Builder: Turn random, mismatched ingredients into target-aligned meals in 3 seconds flat.
Grocery Waste Monitor: Receive active background alerts for fragile items right before they spoil and cost you cash.
Zero-Effort Nutrition: Clear your physical fitness targets with the macro algebra entirely pre-solved.

After a long day, figuring out dinner shouldn't require executive-level problem-solving.

Stop tracking. Start automating.
